Game difficulty screens

Each of the six daily-session games, and every difficulty dial from the design notes (docs/redesign-v2/research/2026-11-12_difficulty-design-notes.md), shown at the levels where it changes. Dashed cards are dials the notes propose that the game does not have yet.

Levels are today's 1-10 scale, forced with the debug level jumper, at the 360 × 780 design canvas. Timing dials are shown by the phase they control. Tap any screen to enlarge it.

Memory

Shopping List

Recall, Retention

Read a shopping list, walk to the market, and pick the right items off the shelves.

/app/game/market-memory?debugLevel=1-10

List length

3 items → 6 items

More to hold in mind. Six is the most the cart can show.

Wait before shopping

1.5 s → 6.5 s

The list is covered and the cart travels. This hold is the whole time pressure; the list itself is untimed.

Twins on the shelf

off → on

Every list item has a look-alike on the shelf. You must remember exactly what was listed.

One-aisle lists

off → on

Every item comes from one group, such as produce, so they blur together.

How close the twins are

loose → very close

The closest twins are the pulses, which differ only in colour. Proposed, not built.

Not in the game yet

Hints

2 → 0

Each hint highlights one remaining list item on the shelf for 3 seconds. The bulb sits on the left of the cart.

Memory

Station Master

Association, Sequence

You are the station master, sending each train to its own platform.

/app/game/train-yard?debugLevel=1-10

Stations

3 → 4 (5 with new art)

One more pairing to hold. The game always uses 4 today; 3 and 5 are proposed.

Study time

about 9 s → about 3 s

The coloured stations and their names, before they go grey. The player cannot skip ahead.

Pause before sending

1.5 s → 4 s

The blind is down and the pairings must be held in mind.

Stations reveal when filled

on → off

A filled station turns back to colour and cannot be chosen again, which gives away the last answers. Today it is always on.

Similar colours

off → on

Close warm hues in place of four distinct ones. Tests eyesight as much as memory.

Hearts

3 → 2 (maybe 1)

Fewer mistakes before the round ends. Top left of the board.

Attention

Spot Focus

Selective attention, Response speed

A spot-the-difference board: two panels side by side, find what changed.

/app/game/spot-focus?debugLevel=1-10

Number of differences

2 → 6

More to find. Above about 40% of the cells, random tapping starts to work; today's top level has 7 of 12.

How subtle the change is

bold → subtle

Bold swaps in another family, medium a relative, subtle a near twin.

Board size

3 × 3 → 4 × 4

More to scan, and smaller cards on a phone. Today the board stops at 4 × 3.

Mixed subtlety

one level per board → mixed

A board that eases in with mostly bold and one subtle. Proposed, not built.

Not in the game yet

Time limit

none → 90 s

Needed so "how many did you find" can vary. Proposed, not built.

Not in the game yet

Attention

Garden Keeper

Sustained attention, Self-control

Tend a garden: water the flowers when they get thirsty, and leave the wilted plants and pests alone.

/app/game/garden-keeper?debugLevel=1-10

How to play

The legend every round opens with: what to water and what to leave alone.

Plants in the garden

12 → 24 (30 at most)

More to watch.

Share of hazards

25% → 55%

More wilted plants and pests that must not be tapped.

Pace, window and thirsty at once

3 s → 1.2 s; 6 s → 2.8 s; 1 → 3

How often a flower gets thirsty, how long it waits for water, and how many at once. Timing, so a still only hints at it.

Hearts

3 → 3

Top right of the bar. They cap the mistakes the game can record.

Planning

Tiffen Time

Sequencing, Decision-making

Run a tiffin counter: cook what the guests ordered and serve them before they lose patience.

/app/game/serve-guests?debugLevel=1-10

Guests at once and counter size

2 → 4 guests; 3 → 6 dishes

The game always seats 4 guests and lays out 6 dishes today; the smaller starts are proposed.

Dishes per order

1 → 3

Bigger orders. Look at the speech bubbles.

Patience

generous → tight

The bar under each order. Today it is set only by order size.

Uneven patience

none → some guests in a hurry

A real "who first?" question. Proposed, not built.

Not in the game yet

Cooking times

short dishes → long dishes

Long cooks force planning ahead. A cook cannot be hurried.

How long a ready dish lasts

16 s → 9 s

A ready dish glows to be served, then burns if left. Today it lasts 11 s at every level.

Planning

Free Me

Planning, Problem-solving

A sliding-block puzzle: slide the obstacles aside to free the fish.

/app/game/clear-the-way?debugLevel=1-10

Board size

4 × 4 → 6 × 6

More moves available each turn. 6 × 6 is the largest that fits a phone.

Fewest moves and moves before the fish can move

2 → 15-16; 1 → 10+

How far ahead you must think, and how long a chain you untangle before you see progress.

How tightly packed

about 45% → about 75% full

Fewer escape routes. The hardest puzzles come from packing, not size.

Small single-cell blocks

up to 3 → none

Hard to drag, and they let players sidestep the intended chain.

Exit side

right → any side

Supported by the code but never shown or tested.

Not in the game yet
Regenerate with npm run dev then node scripts/screenshot-games.mjs. Everything outside the boards is in docs/flow-screens/.
